target.name: Lumina Vehicles
target.founder: Ahmed Shubber (CEO; Fairfield U double-major mech + biomedical eng), Federico Di Palma (Co-founder)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $8M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Lumina Vehicles is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $8M to date, led by CEO Ahmed Shubber (mechanical and biomedical engineering, Fairfield University). The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable across the robotics and manufacturing sector, including stage-adjacent firms such as Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $8M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, yields $16M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector comparables yields $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $1.8B.

The wide spread between methods reflects fundamental uncertainty in scaling a pre-revenue or early-revenue robotics business. The stage-progression method anchors to demonstrated capital, while peer-median reflects valuations of more mature competitors. A reasonable analytical range is $14M (conservative stage-based floor) to $1.9B (peer-derived ceiling), with a median implied value of $833M. The appropriate valuation depends critically on near-term technical proof points, addressable market clarity, and competitive positioning relative to the named peer set.
